provenance: Independent source audit followed by direct reading and comparison of the immutable packet inputs on 2026-11-01. Shared unit, selection and policy snapshots were read once per identical input across this 25-unit review set. No earlier favorable decision was used as evidence for the conclusion.
rationale: unit:given.patterns introduces the extended syntax, unit:given.state supplies slots/maps, and unit:given.evaluation and unit:given.steps define evaluation and the original Let behavior. Transfer.nil requires no remaining fields, while Transfer.cons selects a named field from any position and transfers its exact Slot, including none. Bind.unpack checks declared class/layout, Nodup pattern field names, Nodup destination names, freshness against all variable keys, and exhaustive Transfer; it removes the single matching object entry and adds exactly the produced bindings without changing nextId. Step evaluates first and then binds. These match the displayed Unpack rule and result. The rule announces declaration order for display; the surrounding pattern prose and Transfer support arbitrary permutations. Class mismatch and occupied-or-empty preexisting destination names cannot satisfy the binding premises. The identity/slot notation has already been introduced before this transition rule.
limitations: This is a correspondence comparison of the frozen prose, exact selected statements/definitions, and identified semantic context. No Lean build, test execution, or proof-tactic audit was performed; compilation and evidence validation are separate checks.

Listed full-source context snapshots were consulted for the supporting declarations and example states discussed in the rationale and dependency comparisons; the listing does not claim examination of every unrelated proof or declaration in those files.
